Done. `out/T5/plan.yaml` merges the adapter and writes the sharded checkpoint.

The plan: `matmul` B@A per layer into `base::merge_tmp.<i>.prod`, assert 12 pairs, `permute [1,0]` (fan_in_fan_out), `scale_ by 2.0` (alpha/r), `add_` into `h.<i>.attn.c_attn.weight`, `delete` the intermediates, then the required asserts and `shard: 100MB` output.

Result: 5 shards + index, 160 tensors, `wte.weight` alone in its own shard, all others ≤100 MiB of tensor data; the 148 untouched tensors are bit-identical and the 12 merged ones match a hand-computed reference to <1e-6 relative error.

Two friction points, both recorded in `out/T5/REPORT.md`: `matmul`'s `from_b` is a rewrite of the `from_a` match (so no regex escapes there), and `assert count ... is: 0` can't express absence — the resolver errors on zero matches first, so the "no `lora_`" check became a negative-lookahead count of 160.
